source.title: Array .min() and .max() throw 'Maximum call stack size exceeded' on large arrays

labels.name: status:in-linear
labels.description: Issue or PR is now in Linear

source.body:
### Bug Description

`Array.min()` and `Array.max()` in expressions throw `Maximum call stack size exceeded` for an array of about 125,000 numbers or more.

Both functions call `Math.min(...value)` / `Math.max(...value)`, which passes every element of the array as a separate function argument. V8 (and QuickJS) put those arguments on the stack, so a large enough array overflows it. `sum()` and `average()` use `reduce` and work on the same arrays.

The same code is in `packages/workflow/src/extensions/array-extensions.ts` and its mirror in `@n8n/expression-runtime`.

### To Reproduce

1. Add a Set (Edit Fields) node with an expression such as `{{ Array.from({ length: 200000 }, (_, i) => i).max() }}`, or call `.min()`/`.max()` on a large numeric array from an earlier node (e.g. `{{ $json.prices.max() }}` with 200,000 prices).
2. Execute the node.
3. The expression fails with `Maximum call stack size exceeded`.

Minimal Node reproduction of the same call:

```sh
node -e 'console.log(Math.max(...new Array(200000).fill(1)))'
# RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded
```

### Expected behavior

`199999`, as for smaller arrays. `.sum()` on the same array already works.

### Debug Info

Found by reading the code on `master`, and reproduced with tests that call `.min()`/`.max()` on a 200,000-element array in the legacy and QuickJS expression engines and on `arrayExtensions.functions.min/max` directly.

### Operating System

Ubuntu Linux

### n8n Version

master (current HEAD)

### Node.js Version

20.19.2

### Database

SQLite (default)

### Execution mode

main (default)

### Hosting

self hosted

comments.author: goutham-valugula
comments.text: I checked both current implementations (`packages/workflow/src/extensions/array-extensions.ts` and the `@n8n/expression-runtime` mirror): each maps the values and spreads the entire result into `Math.min`/`Math.max`. A bounded chunk reduction would avoid the argument-count limit while retaining native `Math.min`/`Math.max` behavior (including `NaN` and signed zero); the existing `ensureNumberArray` validation and string-to-number conversion can remain unchanged. The two copies should be updated together to keep legacy and QuickJS expression behavior aligned.
